section_summary.extract_value: This section describes hierarchical multiple regression analyses testing whether body appreciation predicted unique variance in sexual function (Hypothesis 2) and whether BMI moderated that relationship (Hypothesis 3). Results indicated that, after controlling for age and partner status, body appreciation significantly predicted sexual arousal, sexual satisfaction, orgasm, and overall sexual function, while BMI did not significantly moderate these relationships and Hypothesis 3 was not supported. The section does not report sample characteristics, measures, correlations, or the number of studies.
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences from the provided text: "We used hierarchical multiple regression analyses to test Hypotheses 2 and 3." "BMI did not significantly moderate the relationships between body appreciation and any of the components of sexual function. Therefore, Hypothesis 3 was not supported." "Multiple regression analyses indicated that, after controlling for age and partner status, body appreciation significantly predicted sexual arousal, sexual satisfaction, orgasm, and overall sexual function, therefore supporting Hypothesis 2."

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports hierarchical multiple regression analyses testing Hypotheses 2 and 3: Step 1 entered age and partner status, Step 2 entered body appreciation (BAS), and Step 3 entered the centered interaction body appreciation × BMI; the authors adjusted the p level to .007 to account for multiple tests. The text states that BMI did not significantly moderate relationships (Hypothesis 3 not supported) and that, after controlling for age and partner status, body appreciation significantly predicted sexual arousal, sexual satisfaction, orgasm, and overall sexual function (supporting Hypothesis 2). Table 2 reports these analyses for the sample (n = 246).
